title: Replication Package — When Same-Prompt LLM Source Diversity Doesn't Help: An Ablation of Semantic Mutation Operators in Metamorphic Testing for Single-Output Scientific Computing Kernels
description:
Companion replication archive for the P2 paper submitted to Information and Software Technology (2026). The paper proposes a Semantic Mutation Score (SMS) built on five domain-semantic mutation operators (Conservation, Monotonicity, Convergence, Trajectory, Fidelity-order) and demonstrates via a 12-PUT × 5-MP ablation (60 cells, 292 LLM-generated mutants vs 1,250 cosmic-ray syntactic mutants) that under an identical prompt MR-design, not LLM-source diversity, is the dominant lever on aligned-vs-cross effect size.

Headline numbers reproduced from the cache: Cliff's δ = 0.439 (95% CI [0.13, 0.74]); Friedman χ² = 15.30, p = 0.0041; AST overlap with cosmic-ray = 5.14%; stipulated-alternative power at δ_truth = 0.474 = 49.1%.

Bundle contents: 12 PUTs in src/p2/puts/, 60 MRs in src/p2/mrs/, 37 mutation operators, AVP dispatcher, three-layer LRCA classifier, SMS computation, RQ1–4 statistical analysis, end-to-end campaign scripts, 116-test pytest suite, 5 paper figures, and the Round-1 + Round-2 reviewer reports plus the Stage-4.5 final integrity report.

Reproducibility: Deterministic from the committed cache (SEED=42, temperature=0); no LLM API access required. Three-command quickstart in README.md rebuilds paper_numbers_v4.json + cosmic_ray_12put_ast_diff.json in < 5 minutes. Full pipeline finishes in ≤ 2 hours on a 4-core laptop.
notes: Round-1 and Round-2 reviewer reports plus the Stage-4.5 final integrity report are bundled under docs/review_2026-05-{01,02}/ for audit purposes.
